executive_summary.summary: OpenMRS Core is a Java/Spring/Hibernate medical-record platform holding patient health information. The deep dive found 678 service methods guarded by @Authorized privileges and 9 servlet filters, including a pre-authentication first-run setup wizard and a database update wizard that run outside the normal security stack. Authorization appears to be function-level (privilege) only, with no evidence of patient/location scoping. Authentication, session handling, secrets storage, module trust and deployment posture could not be confirmed from the repo and are carried as explicit open questions. All repo-derived facts are heuristic, low-confidence candidates.
top_risks: Setup wizard can take over an uninitialized or reset instance (T-001).
Function-level privileges do not guarantee patient-level authorization of PHI (T-003).
Dynamically loaded modules run with full platform privileges and no evidenced integrity checks (T-004).
Web authentication/session controls and update-wizard authentication are unconfirmed (T-005, T-002).
Plaintext runtime credentials and legacy dependencies expand the blast radius (T-008, T-010).
key_recommendations: Restrict the setup/update wizards and pre-provision runtime configuration.
Add patient/location-scoped authorization and audit logging of chart access.
Sign and verify modules; move secrets out of the properties file; run SCA and upgrade legacy libraries.

threats.title: Unauthenticated first-run setup wizard can be hijacked to take over a deployment
threats.attack_scenario: While the runtime properties file is missing, InitializationFilter redirects every request to the setup wizard. An attacker who reaches a fresh or reset instance first supplies attacker-controlled DB settings and an admin password, so the instance is owned before the operator completes setup; if the properties file is deleted or unreadable later, the wizard can re-activate.
preconditions: Instance reachable from untrusted network before setup completes
No runtime properties found, or properties lost/unreadable after deployment
threats.impact: Full administrative takeover; data redirected to an attacker database; later PHI exposure.
assumptions: Wizard access control after first run was not read; the Javadoc describes only the redirect-when-no-properties behavior.

threats.title: Database update wizard authentication can be brute forced or its execute step reached without re-verifying the super user
threats.attack_scenario: UpdateFilter prompts for super-user credentials before running Liquibase changesets, outside the normal Spring security stack. An attacker with network access repeatedly guesses credentials with no evidenced lockout, or posts directly to the execute step, and applies or triggers schema changes.
preconditions: Pending database updates exist (after an upgrade)
No lockout/rate limiting on the pre-Spring wizard
threats.impact: Schema tampering, admin account access, availability loss during upgrade windows.
assumptions: Brute-force protection and session re-verification between steps were not confirmed.

threats.title: Function-level privileges do not prove patient/location-level authorization of clinical records
threats.attack_scenario: Service methods are guarded by @Authorized(PrivilegeConstants.GET_PATIENTS/GET_ENCOUNTERS/GET_ORDERS...) which check that the caller holds a privilege, not that the caller may access that specific patient, location or program. Any user holding a read privilege can enumerate or fetch any patient's records by identifier, including through modules exposing REST/FHIR endpoints.
preconditions: User holds a broad read privilege
No per-patient/location/program scoping beyond privileges
assumptions: Only declared annotations were observed; AOP enforcement and any data-scoping logic were not read.

threats.title: Malicious or tampered module executes arbitrary code with full platform privileges
owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
threats.attack_scenario: An attacker with module-management access, or a compromised module distribution source, uploads an .omod that contributes servlet filters, Spring beans and privileges. Modules load in-process with no sandbox, so the module reads the DB, adds users or exfiltrates data.
preconditions: Admin account or module upload path compromised, or unsigned module installed
No signature verification of modules
threats.impact: Complete application and data compromise; persistent backdoor.
assumptions: Module upload authorization and integrity checking were not read.

threats.title: Weak authentication and session management on the web application
threats.attack_scenario: Credential stuffing or brute force against the login endpoint, session fixation, or CSRF against authenticated clinicians succeeds if lockout, session regeneration and anti-CSRF tokens are missing.
preconditions: Login reachable from untrusted network
No lockout, MFA or CSRF protection
threats.impact: Account takeover of clinical users; unauthorized PHI access or order changes.
assumptions: Authentication code was not reviewed; this is a design-pattern risk pending questionnaire answers.

threats.title: Injection via HQL/SQL/Lucene query construction in the persistence layer
threats.attack_scenario: User-supplied search terms (patient name/identifier search, concept search, admin SQL/reporting features) reach Hibernate/HQL or Lucene query parsers via string concatenation or dynamic queries, allowing data extraction or manipulation.
preconditions: Any code path builds queries from unvalidated input
assumptions: No query-building code was read; ORM usage may mitigate most paths.

threats.title: Unauthenticated or unvalidated HL7 message intake enables record injection or parser attacks
owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
threats.attack_scenario: An attacker able to submit HL7 messages inserts forged observations or encounters for arbitrary patients, or sends malformed/XML-bearing payloads to crash or exploit the HAPI parser and queue processor.
preconditions: HL7 intake channel reachable by untrusted senders
No message authentication or schema/size validation
threats.impact: Clinical record integrity loss; patient safety risk; service disruption.
assumptions: Transport/authentication for HL7 intake is not defined in core and may be module specific.

threats.title: Database and admin credentials stored in plaintext runtime properties file
threats.attack_scenario: The setup wizard writes DB connection settings to openmrs-runtime.properties on the host. Anyone with filesystem, backup, container-layer or log access reads DB credentials and connects directly to the database.
preconditions: Read access to host filesystem, image, or backups
threats.impact: Direct database compromise bypassing application authorization.
assumptions: Credential storage format was not read; plaintext is assumed from OpenMRS design.

threats.title: PHI leakage in logs and insufficient audit trail for privileged and PHI-access actions
owasp: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
threats.attack_scenario: Verbose logging of patient identifiers or exception details leaks PHI into log files; absent access logging means unauthorized chart access or privilege denials go undetected.
preconditions: Debug-level logging in production; no audit of read access
threats.impact: Undetected insider snooping and breach; compliance failure.
assumptions: Log content and audit coverage not reviewed.

threats.title: Vulnerable or end-of-life third-party dependencies
threats.attack_scenario: The build pulls ~115 dependencies including the log4j 1.2 bridge, log4j-core, commons-fileupload, c3p0, hibernate-ehcache, jackson-mapper-asl and the legacy javax stack; known CVEs in outdated versions are exploitable through request parsing or deserialization.
preconditions: Vulnerable versions deployed
threats.impact: Remote code execution or DoS depending on component.
assumptions: Specific versions were not assessed; SCA scan required to confirm any CVE.

threats.title: Stored or reflected XSS in JSP/Velocity views exposing clinician sessions
threats.attack_scenario: Patient names, notes, concept descriptions or form content stored by one user render unescaped in JSP/Velocity pages for another, running attacker script in a clinician or admin session.
preconditions: Unescaped output in any view
Missing CSP/HttpOnly
threats.impact: Session hijack; admin takeover via script.
assumptions: Output encoding practices not reviewed.

threats.title: Cleartext transport between users, application and database
threats.attack_scenario: Container exposes port 8080 with no documented TLS termination; JDBC TLS is not evidenced. Network attackers sniff or modify credentials and PHI in transit.
preconditions: Deployment without TLS reverse proxy or JDBC TLS
assumptions: Production TLS posture unknown.

threats.title: Scheduled-task management enables privileged code execution and persistence
threats.attack_scenario: A user with 'Manage Scheduler' can register tasks that reference arbitrary task classes and cron schedules, creating recurring code execution under the application daemon identity that survives restarts.
preconditions: Attacker holds Manage Scheduler privilege or admin session
assumptions: Task class restriction logic was not read.

threats.title: Clinical order workflow trusts client-supplied patient, order and status fields without per-step ownership or state checks
threats.attack_scenario: A clinician legitimately authorized to place orders sends a valid revise/discontinue/fulfil request that targets another patient's order id, or moves a discontinued or voided order back to an active state. Every request is syntactically valid so no injection scanner flags it; patient-safety consequences include wrong medication or lab results.
preconditions: Order endpoints accept identifiers and status from client
Ownership and state-machine checks not re-evaluated at each step
threats.impact: Patient-safety incident; integrity loss of medication/lab orders.
assumptions: Order lifecycle steps were inferred from @Authorized service methods, not from documented workflow.

threats.title: HL7 intake lacks exactly-once and patient-attribution guarantees (replay, duplicate, mis-match)
threats.attack_scenario: A replayed or deliberately duplicated HL7 message creates duplicate or conflicting observations; ambiguous patient-matching keys let a forged message attach results to the wrong patient with no reconciliation control.
preconditions: No message id dedupe or sender authentication
Patient-match keys taken from message body
threats.impact: Wrong-patient clinical data; downstream decisions on corrupted records.
assumptions: Matching and dedupe logic not read.

attack_paths.title: Internet attacker takes over a fresh or reset instance through the setup wizard
required_weaknesses: Setup wizard reachable and unauthenticated while properties are missing
recommended_controls: Restrict the wizard to localhost or a one-time setup token
Pre-provision runtime properties in automated deployments

attack_paths.title: Authenticated clinician enumerates patient charts through function-level-only authorization
recommended_controls: Audit and alert on bulk chart access

attack_paths.title: Compromised admin or module source installs a backdoor module that reads the database
required_weaknesses: Module upload accessible to a compromised admin
attack_paths.impact: Persistent full compromise with direct DB access.
recommended_controls: Allowlist module sources and restrict upload

attack_paths.title: Host or backup access exposes runtime properties and leads to direct database compromise
attack_paths.impact: Unrestricted DB access bypassing application controls.
recommended_controls: Use a secret manager or environment-injected secrets

attack_paths.title: Forged HL7 messages write incorrect clinical data for another patient
recommended_controls: Quarantine ambiguous matches for human review

preventive: Disable or bind the setup wizard to localhost after first initialization; require a one-time setup token.
Pre-provision runtime properties in automated deployments so the wizard never activates.
detective: Alert when the wizard is served or runtime properties change.
corrective: Rotate admin and DB credentials; rebuild instance from a trusted baseline.
compensating: Network ACL or reverse proxy that blocks setup paths from untrusted networks.

preventive: Add lockout/rate limiting to the update wizard; re-verify the authenticated super user on the execute step.
Run updates from a maintenance window on an isolated network.
detective: Log and alert on failed wizard logins.
corrective: Restore DB from backup if unauthorized changesets ran.
compensating: Restrict access to the update path by IP allowlist.

preventive: Add patient, location and program-scoped authorization in addition to privileges.
Centralize access decisions in the service layer.
detective: Audit-log every patient chart access; alert on bulk or out-of-care-team access.
corrective: Revoke sessions and notify per breach policy.
compensating: Break-the-glass workflow with reason capture for sensitive records.

preventive: Verify module signatures and restrict upload to a controlled pipeline.
Restrict module-management privileges to a small admin group.
detective: Alert on module install/changes and unexpected servlet filters.
compensating: Run OpenMRS with least-privileged OS and DB accounts.

preventive: Enforce lockout, MFA, session regeneration on login, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens.
corrective: Force password reset and revoke sessions.

preventive: Use parameterized HQL/SQL and escape Lucene queries; validate input.
detective: Log and alert on query errors/anomalies.

preventive: Authenticate HL7 senders; validate schema and size; disable external entity resolution.
Move DB credentials to a secret manager or injected environment; restrict file permissions.
detective: Alert on reads of the properties file.
compensating: Encrypt backups and restrict image access.

preventive: Mask PHI in logs; set production log levels; add structured audit events.
Run SCA in CI; upgrade or replace log4j 1.x bridge and legacy libraries.
Context-aware output encoding; Content-Security-Policy; HttpOnly cookies.
Terminate TLS in front of the application; enable JDBC TLS; HSTS.
Restrict scheduler to allowlisted task classes; separate privilege.
detective: Alert on new or changed tasks.
compensating: Run scheduler under a low-privilege identity.

preventive: Re-check patient ownership and order state at each step; enforce a server-side state machine; do not accept status fields from clients.
compensating: Pharmacist verification gate for high-risk orders.

preventive: Deduplicate by message id; authenticate senders; quarantine ambiguous patient matches.
detective: Reconcile counts between queue, archive and errors.

sast_recommendations.scan_recommendation: Find service and controller methods that read or modify patient-scoped data without an ownership/location check, and @Authorized-style annotations used as the only gate.
Trace request inputs into Hibernate createQuery/createSQLQuery calls and Lucene QueryParser use.
Find unescaped output of stored or request data in JSP/Velocity templates and controllers.
Check state-changing endpoints for CSRF tokens and login flows for session id regeneration.
Find writes of passwords to properties files and hardcoded connection strings or keys.
Check XML/HL7 parser configuration for external entity resolution and Java deserialization of untrusted data.
Find class loading, reflection and file-write paths in the module loader and scheduler task instantiation lacking allowlists or integrity checks.

sast_recommendations.focus_area: Sensitive data in logs and missing audit logging
sast_recommendations.scan_recommendation: Find logger calls that include patient objects or credentials, and service methods lacking audit events.
Manual-review/custom rule focus: order save/discontinue/fulfil paths accepting status or ids from callers without state/ownership re-checks. No catalog query exists for this class.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify the setup wizard is not reachable on an initialized instance and cannot be re-activated.
high_level_steps: On a non-production initialized instance, request setup wizard paths without authentication.
Verify access is denied or redirected.
On a staged fresh instance, verify wizard access is restricted to the intended network.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Setup paths return denial/redirect once initialized; fresh-instance wizard is network restricted.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Do not run against production; never submit real DB credentials to a wizard under test.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify the update wizard enforces authentication, lockout and step re-verification.
high_level_steps: On a staging instance with pending changesets, attempt unauthenticated access to review and execute steps.
Attempt a small number of invalid logins and observe lockout/throttling.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Execute step is refused without a valid super-user session; repeated failures are throttled.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Staging only; use disposable DB snapshots.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify users cannot read other patients' data outside their location or care team.
high_level_steps: Create two test users with the same read privileges but different locations.
As user A, request patient/encounter/order identifiers owned by user B's scope.
Check response codes and fields.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Access outside the user's scope is denied without disclosing object existence.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Synthetic patients only; no real PHI.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify lockout, session regeneration, cookie flags and CSRF protection.
high_level_steps: Review cookie attributes after login.
Verify the session id changes after login.
Submit state-changing requests without CSRF tokens.
Apply bounded login attempts to test lockout.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Session regenerated, cookies HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, missing CSRF token rejected, repeated failures throttled.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Use test accounts; keep attempt volumes low.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify patient/concept search and filter inputs are not injectable.
high_level_steps: Enumerate search inputs.
Send benign malformed characters and check for errors/behavior differences.
Use an authorized DAST scanner in a test environment.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Inputs treated as data; generic errors only.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Avoid destructive payloads; test DB only.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify stored and reflected data is output-encoded and CSP present.
high_level_steps: Store benign marker strings with HTML metacharacters in name/note fields.
View them as another user and inspect rendering and CSP headers.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Markers render as text; CSP and HttpOnly present.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify unauthenticated senders cannot submit HL7 and malformed messages are rejected safely.
high_level_steps: Identify the HL7 intake channel on a test environment.
Submit a well-formed test message without credentials.
Submit oversized/malformed samples at low volume.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Unauthenticated sender rejected; malformed input routed to error queue without crashes.

dast_recommendations.test_name: Order workflow sequencing and ownership testing
dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify order steps re-check ownership and state.
high_level_steps: Create test orders for two patients.
Attempt to revise or fulfil an order using another patient's order id.
Attempt to revise a discontinued order.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Cross-patient and invalid state transitions are denied.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify HTTPS-only access, strong TLS and security headers.
high_level_steps: Scan TLS configuration of the externally exposed endpoint.
Check HSTS, CSP and cookie headers.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: TLS 1.2+ only, HSTS and security headers present.
